svg.text: Everyday English - Vocabulary
grasp
US /ɡræsp/
MEANING
To understand an idea, especially one that initially
seems difficult or unfamiliar.
IN CONTEXT
I grasp the basic argument, but I am not convinced by
the evidence.
USAGE NOTE
Grasp an idea, principle, implication, or concept.
Understanding an argument does not mean agreeing
with it. I cannot quite grasp it sounds less absolute
than I do not understand anything. The noun a grasp of
describes understanding: She has a solid grasp of the
subject.
CONVERSATION
A: Do you grasp how the new system works?
B: I grasp the principle, but the setup still confuses me.
A: Shall we work through one example?
B: Yes, that would help me connect the steps.
YOUR TURN
Distinguish understanding from agreement. Model: I
grasp your argument, although I disagree with your
conclusion. Then write one sentence using a solid
grasp of.
